method: Scope was assigned only where a publisher or university record described the work's treatment in enough detail to distinguish an edition from a thematic study. Titles alone and third-party summaries were not treated as sufficient evidence.
policy: These notes support work-level scope classification only. They make no claim about complete object extraction, preferred readings, identity, rights, or permission to reproduce text or images.

entries.finding: The Bar-Ilan University abstract says the study gives a new edition of IM 76106 and an edition of a parallel bowl in a private collection, with lexical and phonological analysis.

The Cambridge extract identifies IM 9726, says that a complete translation can now be offered, and notes the article's republication of the Pearson bowl; the SOAS institutional copy is the complete nine-page article.

The Gorgias Press contents enumerate description of one bowl and inscription, palaeographic remarks, text and translation, division of the text, and line-by-line content.
The Brill chapter preview frames a comparative study of incantation-bowl iconography in light of Talmudic descriptions rather than an edition of a single object or bounded corpus.
